Jiang Bolao deduced the culprit's identity, but the suspect ran fast. In the end, I spent an hour chasing him in this old clunker before I finally caught him.
Afterward, I got five speeding tickets.
En.140092500: Second one… a locked-room murder on a cruise ship.
En.140092600:
The real culprit was an animal tamer from the Middle East who could control venomous snakes by playing a flute. He had a snake crawl through the ventilation duct into the room and bite the victim.
In the case notes, Jiang Bolao called this case ridiculous. I agree with him now.
En.140092700: I read through many more case files, and as I do, the past adventures Jiang Bolao and I shared gradually come back to me.
En.140092800: Until I reach the very last sheet of paper in the folder.
En.140092900: This one looks like a character profile. It even has a big headshot of me on it. In the photo, I'm wearing the same trench coat I have on now, my expression serious
En.140093000:
Is this about me?
Frowning, I read the words aloud:
En.140093200: His father had been a detective. After growing up, he took over the family's detective agency.
En.140093300:
He's read a lot of detective novels, so he longs for adventure and wants to run the agency well, but he himself has no talent for detective work?
… Why does it say that about me?
En.140093400: Troubled by this, he meets the protagonist of this story and recruits him into the agency.
En.140093500: Qian Lucai is physically strong, can drive, and handles the agency's finances, but because of that he's a bit stingy with money…
En.140093600: Even so, as the agency's boss and the protagonist's reliable assistant, he plays an important role in the story.
En.140093900: I feel a strange sense of familiarity, but I can't quite put my finger on it.
En.140094000: Frowning, I pinch the corner of the paper between my fingers and fiddle with it.
En.140094200: I know what this is--During the outlining stage, some diligent authors prepare this kind of material in advance.
En.140094300: They compile the character's life story, background, and so on into this document so that, later in the writing process, they can better grasp the character's personality.
En.140094400: In acting as well, excellent performers prepare a character biography for the same reason.
En.140094500: I'm quite familiar with it, because whenever I used to get ready to go on stage, that person would help me put together a character bio for my role.
En.140094600: Thinking of this, I flip the paper over. Just as I expected, in a corner on the back there's some strange writing:
En.140094700: I've encountered some things outside of the script.
En.140094800: The originally chosen lead abandoned that wish, and you took it up. From that moment on, you too became the protagonist of this story.
En.140094801: I don't think the one who prepared so much for this stage ever anticipated that.
En.140094802: With only your usual performance on stage to rely on, you may feel at a loss in the current situation.
En.140094803: But don't worry. To make this PERFORMANCE even more exciting, I've given you a little help.
En.140094804: Use the wish in your heart to interpret your role, and let it shape this story.
En.140094805: Beside this passage is a drawing of a strange red flame.
En.140094807: I still can't fully grasp the meaning of these words, but a voice deep inside tells me they're very important.
En.140094808:
"The one who prepared so much for this stage", huh…
If it really is… him…
En.140094809: I take a deep breath and carefully read through everything written in the document once more.
En.140094900: I think I know what to do.
En.140095100: I follow the same path back to the villa and return to my room.
En.140095200: Just as we agreed, Jiang Bolao is still waiting for me here.
En.140095300: When he sees me come back, he lifts an eyebrow at me.
En.140095500: … There were a lot of documents in the car. I read through all of them. It took some time.
En.140095600: But thanks to that, I've pretty much remembered everything from the past.
En.140095800: Jiang Bolao looks me up and down in disbelief.
En.140096200: Jiang Bolao furrows his brow, lowers his head, and takes a puff from his pipe.
En.140096300: Then he shakes his head and smiles again.
En.140096500: That saves us a lot of explaining later.
En.140096700: What about you? What have you been doing?
En.140096800: Knowing how restless Jiang Bolao usually is, I'm sure he used the time I was away to snoop around and gather intel.
En.140096900: Sure enough, he takes another puff from his pipe and says smugly:
En.140097000: While you were gone, I took a walk around and got the lowdown on the other invitees.
En.140097200: Information on other competitors… Sounds pretty useful stuff.
En.140097300: That wealthy magnate only invited the social elites he was interested in, right? So there shouldn't be many people.
En.140097400: Not many. Including us, there are only two others.
En.140097600: He's choosing an heir, not throwing a party. It's normal there aren't many people.
En.140097700: Besides, fewer competitors is a good thing for us, isn't it?
En.140097900: Do we know any of them?
En.140098000: Funny you mention it--we do. And not just that: one of them is our sworn rival.
En.140098200: Someone who fits that description… Hmm…
En.140098400: How did someone like him get invited?
En.140098500: He's at least a police captain. It makes sense he'd get an invitation.
En.140098600: … Still, he dumps all his cases on us and always looks so mean.
En.140098700: I don't think he fits the "social elite" label no matter how high his rank is.
En.140098800: There, there~ I know you don't like him.
En.140098900: But we'll be living under the same roof for the next few days. You'll have to bear with it.
En.140099100: What about the other one? Do we know them?
En.140099200: We haven't met him, but he's quite famous. He's a doctor.
En.140099300: His family is also very wealthy--on par with the magnate who invited us.
En.140099400: But apparently, he didn't inherit the family fortune. Instead, he opened his own clinic.
En.140099700: …That clinic on King's Avenue? The one with the rare tricolor Border Collie?
En.140099800: Yeah. Can't believe you still remember him.
En.140099900: Mm. We pass by there whenever we go to the library to do research.
En.140100000: That's downtown. Property prices are sky-high, and that clinic is huge and privately owned.
En.140100100: Every time I see it, I just wonder… how much did that cost…
En.140100200: Pfft… Why do you always go straight to money?
En.140100300: Occupational habit, from managing our finances for so long. After all, it's someone's fault for burning through so much cash on every case.
En.140100400: Maa… You work so hard, boss.
En.140100500: Jiang Bolao shakes his head and offers a few perfunctory words of comfort.
En.140100600:
I roll my eyes at him.
Sensing that his remark only annoyed me more, Jiang Bolao quickly changes the subject.
En.140100700: Anyway, should we go visit our competitors?
En.140100800: We'll be staying together for the next few days. It's probably better to go say hello first, right?
En.140101000: Fine, fine. Then who should we go see?
En.140101100: Either one. Whoever you want to meet first.
En.140101200: When you were unconscious yesterday, the villa's butler said the rules for the inheritance contest would be announced at lunch today.
En.140101300: There's still plenty of time before lunch. We can go say hello to both of them.
En.140101500: So who should we go see first?
En.140101700: After walking west down the corridor for a while, we stop in front of a room.
En.140101800: Seeing the door with the sign 201, I can't help frowning.
En.140101900: Because once I knock on this door, I'll have to see that grumpy face again. So annoying.
En.140102000: After I stare at the door for a while longer, Jiang Bolao finally speak up.
En.140102400: If you really don't want to see him, we can bail for now.
En.140102500: … Anyway, we should at least say hello to him. Otherwise, during lunch, he'll definitely--
En.140102800: The corner of my mouth twitches. I turn my head.
En.140102900: Sure enough, that familiar hyena is raising an eyebrow at me.
En.140103100: Oh my, and the great detective is here as well!
En.140103200: Why are the top two from the Beaten Wings Detective Agency blocking my door? Suspecting me of murder?
En.140103400: To be honest, I don't really want to talk to him.
En.140103500: Jiang Bolao, however, plays along smoothly, answering his sharp question with a smile:
En.140103700: We're strangers in this snowy mountain manor. Isn't it normal for us to say hello to an old friend?
En.140103900:
I know you're up to no good.
Spill it. What little scheme are you planning now?
En.140104000:
Let me warn you--I've got my eye on you.
If you pull any more illegal stunts, I'm filing an arrest warrant the moment I get back.
En.140104200: Heh. Brushing the grey area once or twice isn't illegal, but doing it a hundred times definitely is.
En.140104300: If you two annoy me again, even if I can't find a proper charge, I'll still lock you up.
En.140104400:
Do whatever you want.
I think you're just jealous that we always solve the cases before you.
En.140104500: … I couldn't care less about your reckless way of solving cases.
En.140104700: This hyena's name is Yan Liaoliao. He's the police captain for the Bellen Street.
En.140104800: In detective stories, it's a standard trope that the "detective" and the "police officer" don't really get along, and this story naturally follows suit.
En.140104900: As a captain, Yan Liaoliao looks down on the methods we use to solve cases--methods that often skirt the edge of the rules.
En.140105000: And we're equally annoyed by his constant interference. More than once, his obstruction has almost made us miss a clue right under our noses.
En.140105100: In some respects, we really are "sworn rivals".
En.140105200: And since his attitude isn't exactly pleasant, I don't hold back on the sarcasm:
En.140105300: Captain Yan, aren't you the one who prides himself on being upright and incorruptible, the one who looks down on greedy detectives like us who only help people for money?
En.140105400: So why have you now accepted a rich magnate's invitation and come here to fight over some inheritance?
En.140105600: Yan Liaoliao gives me a look.
En.140105700: I'm not particularly interested in winning the inheritance.
En.140105800: I work myself ragged all year long like a spinning top, and on top of that, I have to deal with all the messes you two make. I'm exhausted.
En.140105900: So I just wanted an excuse to get away from work and come here to rest.
En.140106000:
If I happen to get the inheritance, then great, I can retire early.
But even if I don't, a nice, comfortable vacation on this snowy mountain is fine too.
En.140106100: Maa, that's a good attitude, I suppose.
En.140106200: But who knows? Maybe this time you'll finally win against me.
En.140106300: What do you mean, "maybe this time"? "Finally"? Have I lost every other time?
En.140106400:
And besides, great detective, why do you seem not very interested in the inheritance this time?
That's not like your usual style.
En.140106500:
A massive inheritance is just too dreamy. It doesn't feel real.
So we just came to see the sights, not really interested in winning the inheritance itself.
En.140106600: Besides, in my experience, an inheritance left to some lucky stranger only ever shows up in two kinds of stories.
En.140106800: One is a fairy tale. The curious soul who inherits it suddenly turns their life around.
En.140106900: The kind one instantly becomes rich, respected, and lives happily ever after.
En.140107100: Jiang Bolao shrugs and points at himself.
En.140107200: The other, of course, is a mystery detective story.
En.140107400: Everyone will start killing each other over the inheritance, and then have to find the culprit.
En.140107500: Huh? You mean that kind of…
En.140107800: A "closed-circle-of-suspects mystery" is a classic setup in detective fiction.
En.140107900: Simply put: a group of people gather in an enclosed environment and, because of some accident, find they can't leave.
En.140108000: In this isolated, sealed setting, murders happen one after another--until the culprit is caught, or everyone dies.
En.140108100: I've read quite a few detective novels with Jiang Bolao. This kind of case shows up everywhere.
En.140108200: The classic settings are sealed rooms, isolated islands, trains, cruise ships…
En.140108300: And, of course, "a manor in a blizzard".
En.140108500: Honestly, Jiang Bolao and I have solved plenty of cases, but we've never run into one this complicated.
En.140108600: Given the old rule that "wherever a detective goes, trouble follows", I'm inclined to think something really will happen.
En.140108700: With that in mind, I can't help joking:
En.140108800: Maybe by the time dinner's over, there'll be a blizzard.
En.140108900: Then everyone will be trapped here.
En.140109100: I think it's pretty likely too.
En.140109200: Above all, the mood has already set. It would almost be strange if nothing happened, right?
En.140109400: Officer Yan glares at both of us.
En.140109600: Can't we just tour the place in peace, decide who gets the inheritance, and call it a day? Why does someone have to die?
En.140109800: Without a case, what's the point of a detective's existence?
En.140110000: Jiang Bolao steps forward, getting right up in Officer Yan's face.
En.140110100: The guests this time all have pretty interesting backgrounds, don't you think?
En.140110200: A private eye, a police officer… and the guy next door is a doctor.
En.140110300: With a lineup like this, isn't it only natural for something to happen?
En.140110500: The hyena snorts and takes a step back.
En.140110700: Only people like you would wish for something like that.
En.140110800: I'm going back to rest. Don't bother me again.
En.140110900: With that, he slams the door shut with a thud.
En.140111000: Seeing him choke like that, I can't help laughing.
En.140111100: Pfft. He still can't beat us in a war of words.
En.140111200: After all, after so many years as detectives, our words have helped us dig up tons of clues.
En.140111300: Someone as straight-laced as Officer Yan can't keep up.
En.140111600: By the way, about what you said… You really think something will happen here?
En.140111800: The stage is set. No one can leave before the performance is over.
En.140112000: He rubs his pipe, thinks for a moment, then sighs.
En.140112100: Ah, forget it. Let's not get into that now.
En.140112200: Want to go look around somewhere else?
En.140112400: After walking west down the corridor for a while, we stop in front of a room.
En.140112500: The sign on the door reads "204" -- This must be the doctor's room.
En.140112600: … I can't help feeling a little nervous.
En.140112700: It's normal to feel nervous before seeing a doctor, right?
En.140112800: But we're only here to visit, not for an actual consultation…
En.140112900: Maa, it's pretty much the same, isn't it?
En.140113000: In fact, I was even thinking of asking the doctor to take a look at your head, just to make sure nothing was wrong.
En.140113100: I mean, I already remembered everything…
En.140113200: But for the sake of safety, it still worth checking, right? After all, the head is one of the most important parts of your body.
En.140113400: Although it annoys me a bit, Jiang Bolao has a point.
En.140113500: So I don't hesitate anymore and simply reach out to knock on the door.
En.140113700: A cold, indifferent voice comes from inside.
En.140113800: I exchange a glance with Jiang Bolao, then take hold of the doorknob--
En.140114000: The layout of room 204 isn't much different from mine. It seems like every guest room in this villa uses the same decor.
En.140114100: The doctor--a tricolor Border Collie--sits in front of a small table in the center of the room.
En.140114200: When he sees the two strangers who have entered, his eyebrows rise slightly in surprise, but he quickly regains his calm expression.
En.140114300: He stands up and gives us a polite nod.
En.140114500: If I am right, you two must be the director and the lead private eye of that detective agency on Bellen Street.
En.140114600: I'm surprised to hear him identify us so accurately.
En.140114700: Have you heard of us before?
En.140114800: Yes, I have read about your exploits in the newspapers.
En.140114900: And I believe you probably know a bit about me as well.
En.140115000: Maa, after all, everyone who received an invitation is a member of high society.
En.140115100: If we're both fairly well known, it's quite reasonable that we've heard of each other.
En.140115300:
In those newspapers, I saw detailed information about the two of you.
If I remember correctly, the director is called Qian Lucai, and the private eye is called Jiang Bolao.
En.140115600: For the sake of mutual understanding, I will briefly introduce myself as well.
En.140115700: The Border Collie adjusts his gold-rimmed glasses.
En.140115800: I am Luo Luo'ai, a doctor who currently runs a private clinic. I believe you two have passed by it during your investigations.
En.140115900: We certainly did. Our director was just saying earlier that every time he passes by, he couldn't help-- Ouch.
En.140116000: I pull my elbow back from Jiang Bolao's side, glare at him, then add smoothly:
En.140116100: Couldn't help praising how clean and professional the clinic looks like. It's the kind of place that puts any patient at ease.
En.140116300: My clinic can treat all kinds of illnesses, so you are welcome to visit if needed.
En.140116400: … That sounds weird, like you're wishing for us to get sick.
En.140116500: Just a harmless little joke. Of course, as a doctor, I would rather wish for both of you to stay healthy.
En.140116600: How odd his way of speaking is...
En.140116700: I glance over at Jiang Bolao. He doesn't seem particularly bothered by it. Instead, he steers the conversation toward our real purpose.
En.140116800: Speaking of which, we might actually need to ask Dr. Luo for a small favor right now.
En.140116900: Oh? Is one of you feeling unwell?
En.140117000: Jiang Bolao reaches behind me and gives me a small push forward.
En.140117100: Well, we got into a minor car accident on the way here. My boss lost consciousness for a while and had some temporary memory loss because of it.
En.140117200: If it's convenient for you, would you mind giving him a quick check-up?
En.140117400: Dr. Luo pushes up his glasses and gives me a careful once-over.
En.140117500: He pulls the chair he'd been sitting on over in front of me and gestures for me to sit.
En.140117700: I obediently sit down. Memory loss is pretty scary, so it would be best if I could get a quick check and make sure everything is fine.
En.140117800: Dr. Luo pulls a small penlight out of his inner coat pocket as he asks:
En.140117900: Since you woke up, have you experienced any dizziness, blurred vision, or nausea?
En.140118100: I see… So there are no obvious symptoms.
En.140118200: Speaking of nausea... I realize I haven't eaten a single thing since I arrived at the villa. I am getting a little hungry.
En.140118300: While I am lost in thought, Dr. Luo steps in front of me. He reaches out and cups my face.
En.140118500: Pardon me. This is purely for the examination.
En.140118600: He aims the penlight at my eyes and clicks it on.
En.140118800: Mmm… Pupil constriction is normal. For a feline kemono, that rules out quite a few possibilities.
En.140118900: Dr. Luo puts away the penlight and says to both me and Jiang Bolao:
En.140119000: Based on the current examination, I believe this gentleman is fine.
En.140119100: If you would like a more thorough examination, you can come by my clinic after this event. I will give you both a special discount.
En.140119300: I frown, stand up, and straighten my clothes.
En.140119400: While I'm doing that, Jiang Bolao has already started chatting with the doctor again.
En.140119500: By the way, Dr. Luo, what made you decide to accept the invitation and come to this villa to compete for the inheritance?
En.140119600: Hearing this, Luo Luo'ai shakes his head.
En.140119700: I have no real interest in the inheritance itself. After all, I do not need to inherit a large fortune.
En.140119800: Tch. Typical insufferably wealthy person talk.
En.140119900: I came here simply to try to make some new friends.
En.140120000: After all, since the invitations were only extended to people the magnate found interesting and distinguished, I figured everyone here would be worth getting to know.
En.140120100: So you're saying that you truly have no interest in the inheritance?
En.140120200: That is correct. Unlike you two.
En.140120300: That's quite a thing to say… I mean, we're not here for the inheritance either.
En.140120400: Mm-hmm~ We heard that there are some rare treasures collected here, so we just wanted to take a look.
En.140120500: As for the inheritance--Well, it would be great if we got it, but it's not a big deal if we don't.
En.140120700: Dr. Luo gives us a serious once-over, then finally shakes his head.
En.140120800: Your actions don't exactly scream "no interest" in that sort of thing…
En.140120900: And you two are partners, which means you have the advantage in numbers. So if you really decided to play dirty, that would be pretty dangerous for me.
En.140121100: In traditional detective novels, the private eye himself is never the culprit.
En.140121400: Please forgive me for being this way, but in this kind of environment, I think I need to remain cautious until we have truly opened up to each other.
En.140121500: "This kind of environment"? What do you mean?
En.140121600: A closed-off villa full of a wealthy man's inheritance, and a group of invited guests who are strangers, yet somehow seem connected to each other…
En.140121700: No matter how you look at it, it is a dangerous environment.
En.140121800: Mm-hmm, you're very perceptive. That's a good thing.
En.140121900: I see… If you put it that way, it really is dangerous.
En.140122000: But at least, since you just helped me with that check-up, if I were to do anything bad, I definitely wouldn't go after you first.
En.140122100:
And if something happens to you, I'll come help you.
Don't underestimate me. I'm strong in a fight, so I can definitely protect you.
En.140122300: Anyway, until we have built up enough mutual trust, I would prefer to keep to myself.
En.140122400: If you two have any plans, I will neither interfere with nor obstruct them--but for now, I will not offer any assistance either.
En.140122500: Unless it is important, please try not to disturb me. Thank you very much for your understanding.
En.140122600: No problem. Please get some good rest.
En.140122700: Jiang Bolao and I give the doctor, who has sat back down in his chair, a small bow before stepping out of his room.
En.140122800: The way he speaks is a bit strange, and he seems pretty cold…
En.140122900: But honestly, he seems like a decent guy.
En.140123000: After all, he's a rich young doctor. Theoretically his character can't be that bad.
En.140123200: But according to what he said… If there really is a culprit willing to do anything for the inheritance, then he's probably the one in the most danger.
En.140123400: A doctor--someone who can treat illnesses and examine causes of death--would typically be taken out first.
En.140123600: But didn't you promise just now that you'd save him, my dear boss?
En.140123700: I can just give him a little help.
En.140123900: Getting jealous over something like that would be way too lame—
En.140124000: Come on. Let's go look around somewhere else.
En.140124400: After briefly visiting our two neighbors, Jiang Bolao and I take another stroll around the villa.
En.140124500: I have to say, this magnate is truly loaded—so loaded that he has an entire exhibition hall on the second floor dedicated to displaying his collection.
En.140124600: That hall even contains treasures from other countries. I spot artifacts from the Land of the Rising Sun.
En.140124700: According to the description, they were gifts from a close friend of the magnate--the young master of a fox-clan merchant family from that country.
En.140124800: Yeah, they're all enviable big shots, filthy rich.
En.140124900: Thinking about this, I can't help but sigh.
En.140125000: Hearing me sigh, Jiang Bolao turns his head curiously:
En.140125200: I was just thinking--even if we solved eight hundred cases, we still probably couldn't afford a single artifact from that hall. It almost makes me resent the rich.
En.140125300: Maa, maybe we'll win the inheritance contest. Then all of this stuff would be ours.
En.140125400: After all, look at our opponents--They're all slacking off.
En.140125600: Do you really want that inheritance?
En.140125900: I'm not interested in that kind of stuff. Why would you think that?
En.140126100: Ever since we arrived at the villa, you've seemed really excited.
En.140126200: Oh, is that what you mean?
En.140126300: Jiang Bolao takes a puff from his pipe, squinting his eyes and smacking his lips.
En.140126400: It's just that I find the current environment very interesting.
En.140126500: … You're really into the whole "closed-circle-of-suspects" setup?
En.140126600: Fine, I guess that's normal. We've never worked a case like this before. It should be refreshing.
En.140126800: And besides, for our final case, it's more than fitting.
En.140126900: This will be the perfect ending to my detective career—
En.140127200: "The ending to your detective career"? What do you mean?
En.140127300: Oh, right… I forgot to tell you…
En.140127400: Jiang Bolao scratches his mane a little sheepishly.
En.140127600: Once I solve one more case interesting enough, I'll retire.
En.140127700: Retire? What do you mean, you're planning to stop being a private eye?
En.140127900: Why didn't you talk to me about something this big? Why would you--
En.140128100: A crisp chime suddenly rings out, cutting off my questioning.
En.140128200: Jiang Bolao, as if he hadn't heard any of my questions, says in a light, calm voice:
En.140128400: Everyone in this villa will gather together for this feast…
En.140128500: It's bound to be very interesting.
En.140128600: He strides toward the first-floor dining room. Noticing that I'm still standing there, he turns back and crooks a finger at me:
En.140128800: Come on. Put those personal matters aside for now.
En.140128900: Either way, we've got to deal with what's right in front of us, right?
En.140129100: Let's handle the immediate matters first…
En.140129200: Yeah, let's go see what tricks the magnate has set up.
En.140129400: The dining room is a separate room to the east of the first-floor living room.
En.140129500: By the time Jiang Bolao and I arrive, a pale-furred wolf in a waiter's uniform is standing at the entrance.
En.140129600: He respectfully ushers the two other guests inside, then turns to look at us:
En.140129700: Oh! The director of the Beaten Wings Detective Agency, Mr. Qian Lucai, and the great private eye Mr. Jiang Bolao…
En.140129800: Your exploits have spread far and wide--even I, guarding this villa in the snowy mountains, have heard of you.
En.140129900: He bows to us, then extends a hand toward me:
En.140130000: It's an honor to serve you both today.
En.140130100: This obviously overflattering speech makes me a little uncomfortable.
